name: Florists and gifting (incl. luxury gifting and corporate gifting)

problems.words: Flowers wilt before we sell them and we throw away a lot
quick_ideas: Record what you throw away by stem type for one week, because it shows what you over-buy
Compare buying with what was actually sold, because buying by feel drives wastage.

workzap_build.text: a flower buying planner from past sales and pre-orders, with a wastage log by stem type.

problems.ask_first: Where do your flowers come from?
problems.free_stops: the buying method is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare which stem types wilt in the bucket with which stem types actually sell that same week, so buying stops favouring slow movers.
Give one person the job of writing each day's oldest flowers on one visible list, so staff sell those stems before fresher stock.

problems.words: Instagram, WhatsApp, website and Talabat orders all come separately and we miss some
quick_ideas: Put every order from every channel onto one list for a day, because it shows which channel leaks
Make one person own incoming orders, because shared phones lose them.

workzap_build.text: one inbox for all channels creating a single job card with design, delivery slot and status.

problems.free_stops: channel connections and job-card design go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many orders arrive from each channel during one busy day and how many nearly got missed, so the riskiest handoff stands out.
Give one person each shift the job of writing every new order into one notebook, so no channel waits for someone to remember it.

problems.words: Wrong card message or wrong address on the delivery
quick_ideas: Have the customer send delivery and card details themselves rather than staff retyping them, because copying causes mistakes
Check recent errors for where they began, because the pattern repeats.

workzap_build.text: a confirmation step where the customer enters card and delivery details directly; pi never handles recipient details.

problems.ask_first: How are card messages captured today?
problems.free_stops: the confirmation flow is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note whether recent delivery mistakes came from copied details or rushed handovers, so you target the part causing wrong cards or routes.
Give one person the job of reading the delivery details from one written order slip before dispatch, so card and route mix-ups drop.

problems.words: Same-day orders are delivered late and the occasion is missed
quick_ideas: Look at a busy day's late deliveries by area and slot, because it shows where routing fails
Set a cut-off time for same-day orders, because late orders push others late.

workzap_build.text: delivery routing by area and slot with driver proof of delivery and a live late list.

problems.ask_first: Who delivers, your own drivers or an outside service?
problems.free_stops: routing rules and slot design go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare late same-day deliveries by area with the time each order was accepted, so you spot whether distance or timing causes missed occasions.
Give one staff member the job of grouping same-area deliveries into one handover list each day, so drivers stop crisscrossing and arriving late.

problems.words: Customers want photos before delivery and we forget
quick_ideas: Make the photo part of finishing each order, because it's then hard to skip
Note how many complaints followed a missing photo, because it shows the value.

workzap_build.text: a pre-delivery photo sent to the customer on WhatsApp before dispatch.

problems.free_stops: the photo step setup is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many finished orders left without a photo on one busy day, so you see how often the promise is missed.
Give one person on each shift the job of checking one photo list before dispatch, so customers stop asking where their arrangement picture is.

problems.words: Corporate quotes go back and forth for weeks on WhatsApp and email
quick_ideas: Ask each corporate client for one person who approves, because many voices slow everything
Keep each quote version in one place, because confusion causes rework.

workzap_build.text: a shared page where the corporate client would approve mock-ups, quantities and branding, with every quote version and approval kept on record.

problems.ask_first: How do approvals happen now, WhatsApp, email or both?
problems.free_stops: the approval flow is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many quote versions each corporate order goes through before approval, so you see which clients create the longest back-and-forth.
Give one staff member the job of keeping each corporate quote conversation in one notebook thread, so rework from mixed messages drops.

problems.words: Corporate clients want large branded quantities fast and we can't produce
quick_ideas: Work out how many boxes your team really makes in a day, because it sets honest deadlines
Agree design lock dates with clients, because late changes eat production time.

workzap_build.text: a production board by delivery date showing load against team capacity.

problems.ask_first: Do you bring in extra hands in peak weeks?
problems.free_stops: capacity planning rules go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare how many branded gift units your team planned to finish with how many were actually completed in one day, so deadlines reflect reality.
Give one person the job of writing one daily production list by client and quantity, so the team works from one agreed priority.

quick_ideas: List every unpaid corporate invoice with its age, because it shows who to chase first
Agree payment terms before production, because they're harder after delivery.

workzap_build.text: corporate receivables with ageing and polite reminders sent out.

problems.ask_first: How do you follow up now?
problems.free_stops: terms and reminder timing are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many corporate orders are delivered before a signed approval or purchase note arrives, so weak handovers before billing become visible.
Give one person a daily notebook check for orders awaiting client approval before packing, so fewer bouquets leave before paperwork is complete.

quick_ideas: Count boxes, ribbons and sleeves now against last season's use, because the gap is your order
Ask suppliers their peak lead time, because it sets your real order date.

workzap_build.text: packaging and hamper-item stock with expiry and reorder alerts.

problems.free_stops: reorder levels are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which packaging items run out fastest during busy gift preparation, so you stop being surprised by the same missing pieces.
Give one staff member the job of noting low packaging items in one notebook place each evening, so peak packing keeps moving.

problems.words: Corporate clients don't come back next Eid
quick_ideas: List last year's corporate clients and what occasion they ordered for, because it shows who to approach
Approach them well before the occasion, because budgets are set early.

workzap_build.text: a corporate client calendar of past occasions prompting re-engagement in time.

problems.ask_first: How do you reach past corporate clients now?
problems.free_stops: the re-engagement plan goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which past corporate clients ordered only once and which returned for another occasion, so your Eid follow-up list stops being guesswork.
Give one staff member the job of keeping one notebook page for upcoming corporate occasions, so follow-ups happen before gift budgets move elsewhere.

never_say: Anything that requires recipients' names, addresses, phone numbers or card messages in the chat.
Advice on anti-bribery limits for corporate gifts, or help disguising gifts or splitting invoices.
Advice on flower import permits, phytosanitary rules or food safety of hamper items.
Help supplying alcohol where it is illegal, or any licensing advice.
Help locating a person or getting someone's address without their consent.

sample_reply.person: Before Eid our corporate clients change the design three times and then want hundreds of boxes in a few days. Any solution?
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, this can be brought under control, and the first steps are simple.
First, ask each client for one person who approves, because many voices slow everything down.
Second, work out how many boxes your team really makes in a day, so deadlines you agree are honest.
Workzap's part would be: a page where clients approve designs and quantities with full history, and a production board showing load against your capacity.

Would you like me to arrange a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
